{{nihongo|'''Kawawa Shrine'''|川勾神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sagami Province]].

It is said to be one of the 13 Shikinai shrines in Engi Province (small shrines) in {{ill|Sagami Province|ckb|پارێزگای ساگامی|cs|Provincie Sagami|de|Provinz Sagami|es|Provincia de Sagami|fa|ولایت ساگامی|fr|Province de Sagami|gl|Provincia de Sagami|id|Provinsi Sagami|it|Sagami (provincia)|ja|相模国|ko|사가미국|lt|Sagamio žemė|nl|Sagami (provincie)|pt|Província de Sagami|ru|Сагами (провинция)|simple|Sagami Province|sk|Sagami (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сагами|tr|Sagami (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Саґамі|zh|相模國|zh_min_nan|Sagami-kok|zh_yue|相模國|qid=Q1053732}}. {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=Prefectural company|qid=Q90139226|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}}.A traditional {{ill|José Manuel Balmaceda|Q1322|qid=Q1322|lt=41}}, {{ill|Kokufu-sai|Q11420919|qid=Q11420919|lt=Kounomachi}} is one of the five Sagami shrines that participates in {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ninomiya}}. The main ritual of the festival, ``Zaikan'', is a combination of {{ill|sagamu no kuni no miyatsuko|Q11582190|qid=Q11582190|lt=Aibu}} (Sagamu) and {{ill|Isonaga|Q11481128|qid=Q11481128|lt=Isonaga}} (Shinaga, also written as ``Shicho''), which is the name of Sagami Province. This is said to have been caused by {{ill|Chinese proverbs|Q1210892|qid=Q1210892}}, who fought over whether {{ill|Samukawa Shrine|Q48744|qid=Q48744}} or our company should be designated as Sagami Province {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. The name of the location, ``Ninomiya Town,'' is a nod to our company, and has also been referred to as ``''Ninomiya Daimyojin'''' or ``''Ninomiya Myojin Shrine'''' since ancient times.

=== Enshrined God ===
``Kawagata Shrine Magazine''<ref name="kawawa">``Kawagata Shrine Magazine'' is a bookmark for worship distributed by our company. According to </ref>, the following five deities are currently enshrined.
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Daimyo Takamikoto}} (Onamuji no Mikoto) - The god who cultivated the land of Japan.
* {{jalink|Oimonoimino no Mikoto|Q3270544|Oimonoimino Mikoto} - A god who was instrumental in promoting industry.
* {{ill|Shinatsuhiko|azb|شینات سوهیکو|es|Shinatsuhiko|fa|شینات سوهیکو|ja|シナツヒコ|mni|ꯁꯤꯅꯠꯁꯨꯍꯤꯀꯣ|ru|Синацухико-но ками|sv|Shinatsuhiko|zh|志那都比古神|qid=Q1073925|lt=Class Nagatsuhiko no Mikoto}} (Shinatsuhiko no Mikoto) - God of wind and breath.
* Class Nagatsuhime no Mikoto (Shinatsuhime no Mikoto) - Same as above. A couple deity who pioneered the country of Isonaga.
* {{ill|Princess Sotoorihime|ja|衣通姫|uk|Принцеса Сотоорі|zh|衣通郎姬|qid=Q11626419|lt=Kutori Hime Mikoto}} (Sotohorihime no Mikoto) - A miraculous god who protects safe childbirth."Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 11 Kanto" <ref name="kamigami"> Kenichi Tanikawa (ed.) From "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 11 Kanto" Hakusuisha, December 1984. According to </ref>, "{{ill|Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudoki-kō|Q11503942|qid=Q11503942}} Volume 40" compiled in {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}}12 ({{ill|1841|Q7622|qid=Q7622}}) <ref name="huudo">Edited by Ito Ashida From "Dainippon Topographical Series 15, New Sagami Province Fudoki Draft Volume 2", Yuzankaku, September 1962. In </ref>, there are three deities enshrined: Itsuhime no Mikoto, Omonoki no Mikoto, and Kura Nagatsuhiko no Mikoto, but in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga}} 5th year ({{ill|1776|Q7703|qid=Q7703}}), {{jalink|chief priest|Q1145} 3500}} From the description in the ``Osai-no-Shiki Tradition'', which was transcribed by Mr. Futami, it can be confirmed that {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}} was enshrined in the middle of the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}. Regarding this, "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Sites - 11 Kanto" <ref name="kamigami" It is considered that the enshrining of Hachiman deity was due to the influence of {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|cs|Svatyně Curugaoka Hačiman|de|Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gū|el|Τσουρουγκαόκα Χατσιμάνγκου|es|Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gū|eu|Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gū|fa|تسوروگائوکا هاچیمانگو|fr|Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gū|id|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|it|Santuario Tsurugaoka Hachiman|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|ka|ცურუგაოკა ჰაჩიმანგუ|ko|쓰루가오카하치만궁|la|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|pt|Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gū|ru|Цуругаока Хатимангу|sl|Tsurugaoka Hačimangu|th|ศาลเจ้าสึรูงาโอกะฮาจิมัง|uk|Цуруґаока Хатіманґу|zh|鶴岡八幡宮|qid=Q701403}}, which was worshiped by {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|azb|کاماکورا شوگونلوغو|be|Сёгунат Камакура|ca|Shogunat Kamakura|ckb|زنجیرە شۆگنی کاماکورا|cs|Šógunát Kamakura|de|Kamakura-Shōgunat|el|Σογκουνάτο Καμακούρα|es|Shogunato Kamakura|eu|Kamakura shogunerria|fa|شوگون‌سالاری کاماکورا|fi|Kamakura-shōgunaatti|fr|Shogunat de Kamakura|hak|Kamakura mok-fú|he|שוגונות קמקורה|hu|Kamakura-bakufu|id|Keshogunan Kamakura|it|Shogunato Kamakura|ja|鎌倉幕府|ko|가마쿠라 막부|ms|Kesyogunan Kamakura|nl|Kamakura-shogunaat|no|Kamakura-shōgunatet|pl|Kamakura (okres)|pt|Xogunato Kamakura|ru|Сёгунат Камакура|simple|Kamakura shogunate|sr|Камакура шогунат|th|รัฐบาลโชกุนคามากูระ|tr|Kamakura şogunluğu|uk|Сьоґунат Камакура|vi|Mạc phủ Kamakura|zh|镰仓幕府|zh_min_nan|Kamakura bō͘-hú|zh_yue|鎌倉幕府|qid=Q736839}} and {{ill|Kantō Kanrei|fa|کانتو کانری|ja|関東管領|ko|간토 관령|uk|Канто-канрей|wuu|关东管领|zh|關東管領|qid=Q5367751}}. In addition, among the enshrined deities, Nagatsuhiko-no-Mikoto and Nagatsu-hime-no-Mikoto were originally {{ill|Fūjin|azb|فوجین|de|Fūjin|es|Fūjin|fa|فوجین|fi|Fūjin|fr|Fūjin (divinité)|hy|Ֆուջին|id|Fūjin|it|Fūjin|ja|風神|ka|ფუჯინი|mni|ꯐꯨꯖꯤꯟ|pt|Fujin|ru|Фудзин|th|ฟูจิง|tr|Fūjin|uk|Бог вітру (Японія)|vi|Fūjin|zh|風神 (日本)|qid=Q1483957}}, but it is pointed out that they may have been added because they are connected to ``Shina'' in Isonaga Province.

It is also included in ``Shinto Taikei Shrines Edition 16 Suruga, Izu, Kai, and Sagami Province'' (March 1980), edited by the Shinto Taikei Compilation Association. According to </ref>, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850}}, {{ill|Yurugi district|ja|淘綾郡|pl|Powiat Yurugi|zh|淘綾郡|qid=Q17177016|lt=Yoaya}} and {{jalink|Ashigarashimo County|Q1193172|Ashi It is said that when the east and west coasts of both districts were Isonaga Province, Ayaha Miyatsuko, the ruler of Isonaga Province {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|es|Kuni no miyatsuko|ff|Kuni no miyatsuko|it|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|ko|국조 (일본)|simple|Kuni no miyatsuko|vi|Kuni no miyatsuko|zh|國造|qid=Q2483673|lt=kokuji}}, founded it to protect the country in accordance with an imperial order. ``Shikinaisha Investigation Report Volume 11'' also states that this area was the center of Isonagakuni, and that our shrine was connected to {{ill|Isonagakunizo|Q11481128|qid=Q11481128|lt=Isonagakunizo}} (Shinaga no Kuni no Miyako). According to "Shinhen Sagami Province Fudoki Kou Volume 40" <ref name="huudo" />, the place name ``Kawago'' is said to come from the {{ill|Nakamura River|ja|中村川 (足柄上郡)|qid=Q11365555|lt=Oshikiri River}} flowing in this area in ancient times, and the name of Kawago Shrine is also derived from the place name.Furthermore, “Ninomiyagawa Kojinsha Lucky Book”<ref group="note" name="engi" According to alink|younger brother Tachibanahime|Q11487396|younger brother Tachibana Hime|Q11487396|younger brother Tachibanahime no Mikoto}} (though he was originally from a different tribe) dedicated a sacred treasure, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamato Takeru #Name}}'s wife, Itsuhime no Mikoto<ref>The reason why she is considered the wife of Emperor Konkyo is based on the description in ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}} Volume 13.'' It is said that they prayed for the safe birth of the prince, but ``Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Sites - 11 Kanto'' <ref name="kamigami" /> says that all of this is nothing more than folklore.

In {{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extension}} in 5 years ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), it was elevated to {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi-sha}} and small shrine according to the ``{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}''. It is said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}} made offerings during the {{ill|Former Nine Years' War|Q1187448|qid=Q1187448}} and {{ill|Gosannen War|Q1187411|qid=Q1187411}}."{{ill|Azuma Kagami|Q1042324|qid=Q1042324}}" {{ill|Kenkyū|Q1193933|qid=Q1193933}} 3rd year ({{ill|1192|Q19739|qid=Q19739}}) Article dated August 9th It is said that Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800}} prayed to ``Ninomiya Kawano Daimyojin'' for the safe delivery of {{ill|Hōjō Masako|Q463961|qid=Q463961}}, and {{ill|Shinme|Q11591047|qid=Q11591047}} was dedicated to it. In addition, Minamoto no Yoritomo constructed a shrine building and donated some shrine territory during the Kenkyu era.

Our company was called Ninomiya {{ill|Myōjin|fr|Myōjin|ja|明神|ko|묘진|zh|明神|qid=Q5369590|lt=Daimyojin}}, Ninomiya Myojin Shrine, but from ``Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries'' <ref name="kiso"> edited by the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000. </ref> states that this ``Azuma Kagami'' is the first document that refers to our company as Ninomiya. However, from ``Ichinomiya Nooto Nooto Part 17'' by Moriyuki Saito, ``Ichinomiya Nooto'', Shibunkaku Publishing, December 2002. As pointed out by </ref>, if we follow the Kokufu Festival tradition which states that the origin of 'Zaikan' was the Ichinomiya dispute due to the merger of Sobu and Isonaga, then the Ichinomiya and Ninomiya system existed in Sagami Province in the 7th century, earlier than {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Common theory}}.In the "Ankamonincho Shimomon" dated 4th year ({{ill|1238|Q5433|qid=Q5433}}), there is a mention of ``Ninomiya Kawaso'', indicating that our company's location was {{ill|Shōen|Q1887569|qid=Q1887569|lt=Manor}}. “Basic Research on the Uninomiya System of Medieval Countries” <ref name="kiso" />, the ``Ankamonin Choshitamon'' written in {{ill|Shōka (era)|Q1327489|qid=Q1327489}} 2nd year ({{ill|1258|Q5506|qid=Q5506}}) and the ``{{j alink|Emperor Kameyama|Q360972|Closed Emperor Kameyama}}Insen'' and the descriptions in the ``Kyoto Higashiyama Gobunko Record'' state that while this was a royal manor with strong ties to Kamakura, it can also be seen as {{ill|Kantō goryō|Q11655961|qid=Q11655961}}.

In {{ill|Kenchō|Q1194270|qid=Q1194270}}4 ({{ill|1252|Q5497|qid=Q5497}}), {{ill|Prince Munetaka|Q708897|qid=Q708897}} moved to Kamakura. It is said that when he was sent down, he dedicated a sacred horse to the shrine as a ceremony to mark the beginning of the shogun's life, and an article in "Azuma Kagami" dated April 14, 4th year of Kencho states that he dedicated a sacred horse to a major shrine below Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine.According to the Kawago Shrine Journal <ref name="kawawa" />, the shrine's treasures were destroyed by fire during the {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078|lt=Oei era}} ({{ill|1394|Q6398|qid=Q6398}} - {{ill|1427|Q6305|qid=Q6305}}), leaving only the wooden structure of the shrine. The "Shinhen Sagami Province Fudoki Koko" states that the ancient legend of the area was lost due to this fire.{{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}}4th year ({{ill|1561|Q6618|qid=Q6618}}) {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|Q311080|qid=Q311080}} {{ill|Odawara Castle|Q1013437|qid=Q1013437}} The shrine building was burnt down by the fire of the expedition, but after that {{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064|lt=Motoki year}} ({{ill|1570|Q6659|qid=Q6659}} - Rebuilt by {{ill|Later Hōjō clan|Q431928|qid=Q431928}} in {{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}). According to the Kawago Shrine Magazine <ref name="kawawa" />, our shrine was located in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ushitora}} direction of Odawara Castle, and was especially revered by the Gohojo clan as {{ill|Kimon|Q11673539|qid=Q11673539}} as a guardian deity. According to "Fundamental Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries" <ref name="kiso" />, it is known that during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ar|فترة سينغوكو|arz|فتره سينجوكو|be|Перыяд (unit)|Q855048|stone}} was donated. After that, he was revered by the Tokugawa family, and in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, he would go to {{ill|Edo Castle|Q865913|qid=Q865913}} every year {{ill|Japanese New Year|Q701398|qid=Q701398}} and present {{ill|Ofuda|Q2500908|qid=Q2500908}}, and this continued until the end of the Edo period.

Although the shrine building was severely damaged by a rainstorm in the 9th year of An'ei ({{ill|1780|Q7716|qid=Q7716}}, the priest Futami clan rebuilt it in the 7th year of {{ill|Tenmei|de|Tenmei (Ära)|fa|تنمی|fr|Ère Tenmei|it|Tenmei|ja|天明|ko|덴메이|pt|Tenmei|ru|Тэммэй|simple|Tenmei|sr|Тенмеи|sv|Tenmei|th|เท็มเม|tr|Tenmei|zh|天明 (日本)|qid=Q1194121}} ({{ill|1787|Q7763|qid=Q7763}}), and the shrine remained in use until the early {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} period.In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}6), it was promoted to Gosha, and in {{ill|1932|Q18743|qid=Q18743}} (Showa 7), it was promoted to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. Construction of the current shrine building began after receiving the notification that the shrine would be promoted to a prefectural shrine, but due to the effects of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=World War II}} and the abolition of {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine rank system}} after the war, it was completed 19 years later, in {{ill|1951|Q18591|qid=Q18591}} (Showa 26).

{{ill|2011|Q1994|qid=Q1994}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}23) {{ill|September 21|Q2891|qid=Q2891}} Typhoon No. 15|Q1136789|Typhoon No. 15}} caused damage, including one of the couple's {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=cedar}} falling down on the temple grounds and the roof of the {{ill|Kagura-den|es|Kaguraden|fi|Kaguraden|fr|Kagura-den|it|Kagura-den|ja|神楽殿|qid=Q94498}} being destroyed.

=== Precincts ===
The forest of shrines and temples, mainly consisting of black pine and cedar, is designated as a natural environment conservation area in Kanagawa Prefecture. =Designation status of Kanagawa Prefecture Natural Environment Conservation Area|accessdate=2024-12-05}}</ref>.

=== Cultural property designated by Ninomiya Town ===
* Important {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860}}
** Two wooden standing statues (sculptures) - Designated in March 2007.
** Tabune (archaeological material) - Estimated to be {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}}. Excavated in {{ill|1915|Q2084|qid=Q2084}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}4) from a rice field in the former Shinto territory. Designated on June 5, 1974.
